evidence.claim: Libby Dam rises 422 feet, holding a reservoir that stretches 90 miles upriver, including 42 miles in British Columbia.
evidence.quote: At 422 feet (129 m) in height and a length of 3,055 feet (931 m), Libby Dam created Lake Koocanusa, a reservoir which extends ninety miles (140 km) upriver with a maximum depth of about 370 feet (110 m).  Forty-two miles (68 km) of it is in Canada in southeastern British Columbia.

flags: State commission cache 01 contains only a Wayback wrapper; the catalog’s 2011 Montana designation, mileposts and tribal-consultation condition cannot be verified. Its Alaska designation is also unsupported. Only Forest Service designation used.

Lake naming accounts disagree: Forest Service says contest winner was from Eureka; lake article says Alice Beers of Rexford; dam article claims a treaty origin. Used the Forest Service contest account without a hometown or personal name.

Reservoir dates differ: lake article says damming in 1972, dam article says available for filling in mid-1973, Forest Service says dam completed in 1974. Used 1974 strictly as completion, separate from 1975 dedication.
Dropped the current Tobacco Plains naming story: cache uses unnamed Indigenous people and gives no community source or specific nation for tobacco cultivation.
